item.title: Asmongold's Comments: Streamer rates GTA VI 9/10; criticises Jason Duval's character
item.description: Asmongold sparked debate after claiming GTA VI feels like a “female fantasy” and questioning the writing of male protagonist Jason Duval. During a livestream, he described Jason as a traditional boyfriend who lacks an interesting personality. However, the Twitch streamer clarified that he was enjoying Rockstar's latest release. Despite criticising parts of its story and calling them “femslop,” he rated GTA VI nine out of ten.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Asmongold Rates GTA 6 9/10: Asmongold criticises Jason Duval; says he enjoyed the game
item.description: Twitch streamer Asmongold has called GTA 6 a "female fantasy" and questioned how Rockstar Games has written Jason Duval. During his November 18 livestream, he described Jason as a traditional boyfriend who was not very interesting. However, he made it clear that he was enjoying the game and gave it a 9/10 rating.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: First Gameplay Reactions: Streamers uncover GTA VI glitches; celebrity references spark online talk
item.description: Adin Ross, Kai Cenat, IShowSpeed and xQc were among the first streamers to play Rockstar Games’ GTA VI following its early international release. Their livestreams quickly went viral, featuring unexpected character interactions, gameplay glitches, police chases and bizarre encounters. From IShowSpeed’s shower scene to Adin Ross triggering a three-star wanted level, the streamers’ reactions have added to the excitement surrounding the long-awaited game's release.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Canadian businessman’s $30 million transfers to wife’s caregiver face new trial over alleged gifts
item.description: In a gripping legal battle, a wealthy businessman made a staggering transfer of over $30 million to a caregiver for his ailing wife. Following his passing, the estate argues these transfers were investments, not gifts. The Ontario Court of Appeal has mandated a retrial to reevaluate evidence and the burden of proof, with handwritten notes possibly illuminating the deceased's true intentions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Man once given a home for Christmas now leads charity delivering 29,000 Thanksgiving meals
item.description: Rob Adams, a childhood homelessness survivor, started Thanksgiving Heroes to assist struggling families. Since its launch, the charity has provided more than 29,000 meals in nine U.S. cities. Through collaborations and dedicated volunteers, the organization alleviates the financial strain of Thanksgiving for families. Adams' own experiences fuel his drive to give back, fostering a spirit of community as Thanksgiving Heroes continues to grow.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Virginia court rules on lakeside home disputed by widow and her late husband's children
item.description: A complex legal battle unfolded over a lakeside property in Virginia involving a widow and the children of her deceased husband. The court has decided that the widow retains a fifty percent ownership stake, while her husband’s children will inherit the remaining half. This ruling reversed a prior decision and provided clarity on property rights, paving the way for future partition proceedings while maintaining the widow's current living situation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Partner Loan Remains Payable: Davis forgave family debts; Schriefer’s loan stays due
item.description: The estate of Clive Davis, valued at over $50 million at the time of his passing in June, highlights a complex legacy. His will notably forgives the debts of several individuals while specifically excluding his long-time partner Greg Schriefer from such leniency. After the will was admitted to probate, Davis' impressive Manhattan residence hit the market, adding to his extensive real estate and personal property portfolio.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Rupert Grint wins approval to build 15 homes on former £6 million estate
item.description: Rupert Grint has successfully secured planning permission to create an eco-village at his Kimpton Grange estate in Hertfordshire. This sustainable project will feature six apartments, nine additional homes, a public park, and contribute to local infrastructure improvements, particularly for schools. Earlier concerns from residents regarding wildlife preservation have been addressed, showcasing Grint's commitment to balancing development with environmental care, marking a departure from his previous intent to sell the estate.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Teacher fired for refusing Covid tests wins as court says school board cannot skip dismissal hearing
item.description: Neal Follman, a dedicated teacher from Philadelphia, faced termination after he declined to participate in mandatory Covid-19 testing set by the school district. He challenged this dismissal, claiming that the hearing was improperly conducted. The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled in his favor, underscoring that no elected board members were present during his hearing.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: The Euclid space telescope has spotted 31 ancient quasars, including two record-breakers
item.description: The Euclid space telescope has made a groundbreaking discovery by identifying 31 ancient quasars, significantly contributing to the field of astronomy. Notably, two of these quasars hold the record for their vast distances, originating when the Universe was just 670 million years old. Their light journeyed over 13 billion years to reach Earth, offering unparalleled insights into the early stages of cosmic history.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
